utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, Colonel, of the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good Morning, Colonel. Yesterday when we finished our discussion we were talking about the war diary and the document register which was kept by the command of Operational Group South. Perhaps if we can turn to tab number 10, please where we have a copy of the war diary. And this is 65 ter number 70. Witness, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can briefly explain what this document is.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the war diary. All important orders and decisions must be written down and made into a document. Certain oral orders or orders transmitted orally are recorded in the senior officer's working notebook, which is an official document. Important information reports, any orders received, information on developments obtained from other sources, from duty officers, from any of the relevant bodies, developments important for any unfolding operations, all these are entered into the war diary. Given the fact that I entered most of the information myself, I can confirm that all the developments that occurred during the operation were entered accurately into the war diary, all those that I knew about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we look at the original version of the diary, does your name, your signature appear on most entries on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I've just told you about. I personally entered most of the information. You can see Major Gojkovic, Major Gojkovic's name here too, but he was involved with other assignments later on, whereas Major Skoro would sometimes join me on this task. However, for the most part it was me who was entering the data.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... all important orders and decisions must be written down and made into a document. When you stated that, were you referring to the war diary or some other document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All important orders and decisions in the form of written documents are recorded in the register book which is kept in the general administrations office. It is not necessary for each and every document to be entered into the war diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of practice, any order that you thought was important or report that you thought was important, as well as events, would you have recorded them in the war diary as a matter of general practice?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You referred earlier to an officer's notebook, the senior officer's working notebook. Were all senior officers required to keep a notebook?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The working notebook is an official document. Oral orders or any oral reports are recorded in this working notebook, which is then used as an official document. It is a valid document and it is used to show that an order has been received or a report. However, within the command system everyone must carry out any decisions and orders given by the commander, any tasks set out by any commander. Therefore it is not always necessary for the commander to put this in writing. It is sufficient sometimes to have oral communication, the person receiving the order takes this down in his notebook and acts upon it. This can be done in direct, personal communication, but in addition to this, meetings and briefings may also be held.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The purpose of the officer's notebook, was the purpose to pick up orders that didn't get recorded in a written form to have them recorded in that -- in a written form, in a -- more of a short-form way? Sorry, that question wasn't very good, but is the purpose of the notebook to record orders that perhaps are less formal?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was it the -- was it an obligation for an officer to keep the notebook by rules and -- army rules?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The working notebook is always considered an official document used by every officer to enter. Any sort of information can be used as a memo, as a memo pad. This is where an officer takes notes, any questions or issues being raised, assessments. This is like a memo pad. This is used by an officer to have something to consult later, to remind him of important issues. It's like anything else, but within the system of singleness of command, within the army, the working notebook has an official status and has the status of an official document. What I'm saying is that orders given to subordinate officers may be entered into this notebook and as such may be used as proof of an order being given later on at some later stage. But anything else can be entered. It's up to each individual officer. Mostly these are used as memo pads. Professional plans, weekend plans sometimes are entered into this working notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that more important orders should be formulated as written documents. Was that the practice of the -- the Operational Group Command in Vukovar? Operational Group South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: After -- after an officer retires, what happens to the notebook? Is he required to hand that notebook in to the authorities, the army administration, or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is an obligation, this is a document kept in this administration office, and when people sign out, as it were, for example when retiring, the notebook is returned. For example, I did this in April, as you can see. I'm not sure how long they're kept for though. I've never read that anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can go back to the war diary again, please. And if we can look at the first page with the entry starting the 2nd of October. I see that the entries in the war diary include the date -- sorry, the place, date and time, the description of the event and the signature of the person entering the information as well as a remark. Was that information expected to be recorded in the war diary in relation to events and orders, important orders?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was certainly expected. What these questions mean is if you look at the rules in relation to how war diaries should be kept, this looks perfectly all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you made the entries into the war diary. Was it your responsibility to keep the war diary accurate, as best as you could?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, needless to say. However, as far as the scope of any information entered is concerned, or how far in-depth one goes, it can be a broad range of information, and it can be narrowed down to the bare bones. One thing that is certain, it must be 100 per cent comprehensible and accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The -- you said yesterday that the Guards Brigade Command became the Operational Group Command, Operational Group South, as of the 8th of October. If we can go to that entry in the diary, page 17 in the English, and if we can have look at that, please. The first entry on the page in English. Do you see the entry for the 8th of October, 10 past 8.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not there yet. Bear with me, please. I'm going through the Serbian copy, I think I have just reached the 7th. Right, the 8th. The 8th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... recorded an event and if you can briefly explain what happened on that day in relation to the takeover of Operational Group South.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This piece of information was obviously entered by Captain First Class Skoric, a meeting was held at the OG command, the OG. And then the agenda, number 1, "OG duty takeover. Number 2, preparation and organisation of combat activity. Number 3, other issues. Colonel Bojat thanked everyone for their cooperation and wished them success with thanked everyone for their cooperation and wished them success with their future actions. He focused on some important issues concerning the organisation and conduct of combat operations." You were talking about this box alone, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: From that day forward, from the 8th of October, did the war diary become the war diary of Operational Group South or still the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to provide an accurate response, I would need to have the original order. In which the command of the 1st district organises the system of command and appoints Colonel Mrksic as commander of the first group or rather the command of the brigade as the command of the operations group. I can't specifically remember that order right now, and as far as I remember it was never entered into the war diary, but it must have passed through my hands, it must be somewhere in the register book. The commander must have been told. Or perhaps not, it's really difficult for me to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in any event, after the 8th of October was there any other war diary produced or was this the only war diary?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Earlier you said that to provide an accurate response you would need to have the original order in which the command of the 1st district organising the system of command. Are you referring to the 1st Military District there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. I may have misspoken, but that's what I mean, the 1st Military District. That is the superior command. The superior command of the guards brigade, ever since their arrival in Vukovar, and this had been decided by the federal secretary. I suppose it must also have acted as the superior command of Operations Group South, in view of all the later orders and developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's 65 ter number 70 at tab 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour the war diary will become Exhibit 401.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Colonel, if we can now look at tab 23 and this is a new document that was received after the 65 ter list was submitted and the ERN numbers are English 0467-3069 to 0467-3142, and B/C/S 0467-3122, 0467-3133. Witness, have you found this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The register book. 23, tab 23, is that the one you mean? Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, this register book, is this the document register you were referring to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if we look at the entries in the register book, can you briefly explain what each of the entries mean -- sorry, not each of the entries but the criteria of the entry? On the left-hand side we have number, and then we have the following column, then the degree of secrecy and the date of entry, if you can explain each of the criteria, please, that are recorded in the documents.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The register book contains a number of forms, the forms are standardised and it is clear which kind of information is expected to be entered. If I understand your question, you have the degree of secrecy, date of entering, the name of the sending command and the name of the receiving command, number of document and name of document. The name of document is the address, as it were. It's the name - is this an order? is this a report? - but that's all that's actually stated in the register book. As far as the summary of what the information is about is concerned. Now, according to a logic inherent in all things, if this register book is received by the Chief of Staff, by the chief of the security organ, or by a commander, and there seems to be something that has relevance for the entire operation, this would necessarily be entered into the war diary as well. Or rather, whichever body happens to receive it would probably go through it, this would normally be the commander, and then take appropriate decisions on what to do next. Whether there should be an oral order or if there is a report or some sort of a warning, whether this should perhaps be taken down, each could do this in their own notebooks, but they might as well use the war diary for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So this -- this is the document register that you referred to yesterday that recorded all outgoing and incoming orders and reports; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And by your answer previous, we're talking about written reports and orders?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And this register, whose responsibility -- I think you -- perhaps you haven't. Whose responsibility --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that's written down, every written document is recorded. Not just orders and reports, everything that is sent or indeed received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Whose responsibility was it to keep this register up to date?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of office of the general administration. This is normally attached to the staff and this chief is directly subordinate to the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could Mr. Smith kindly try not to overlap with the interpreters to ensure an accurate record.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I've been told to slow down, which I will. And where was the war diary kept?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war diary was kept in the operations room. It was always kept on the duty officer's table in the operations centre. When things happened and I wasn't there, the duty officer of the operations centre would take down in his notebook any information received while I wasn't present to record this in the war diary. So the only person doing this was the duty officer of the operations centre, and duty officers would normally be the most responsible persons from the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender the document register with the ERN numbers as stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 402, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can now turn to some earlier documents, and if we can turn to tab 8, please, which is 65 ter number 452. Witness, do you have that order in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tab 8. Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That is an order from Colonel General Blagoje Adzic to the Guards Motorised Brigade. Can you briefly state what that order is ordering?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was sent to the command of the Guards Motorised Brigade, but also to the command of the 1st Front. From a terminological point of view, the command of the 1st Military District, that should be somewhere too, not the 1st Front. This strikes me as terminologically erroneous in the norms governing the work of the military structure and organisation; that's how it should be. However, as operations unfold this was obviously at some point renamed the front command. I'm sorry for providing this additional explanation. All in all this document was sent to the brigade command to resubordinate itself by 1600 hours, until the completion of the task, and there is very little I can comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the purpose of this document to resubordinate the Guards Motorised Brigade to the 1st Military District; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order is clear, and it was abided by.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be Exhibit 403, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can look at the next tab, tab 9, which is 65 ter number 453. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, briefly, can you state what the document -- the purpose of document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title reads, "Order on the engagement of officers from the office of the SSNO from the Guards Motorised Brigade." And the order specifies which officers are to be included in what way and when. My comment, this regards the function of control by the superior command in order to gain insight into the situation and the degree of implementation of the tasks distributed. And it was decided that the two officers should be engaged, Colonel Pavkovic and Colonel Terzic. The function of control. In item four it reads, "Submit reports, remarks and recommendations to me intermittently and as needed."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And this document was issued by the Federal Secretariat for the National Defence, the Colonel --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The head of cabinet of the central secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And this was a high-level command than the Guards Motorised Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in your answer it wasn't recorded but the author of this document was -- what was his name?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The author of the document concerning the engagement of officers from the office of the SSNO, it was ordered by the chief or head of cabinet of the SSNO, Colonel Vuk Obradovic and at the time Colonel Nebojsa Pavkovic was his deputy. The Federal Secretariat for National Defence had his own cabinet, his own office, and as far as I can remember, the Guards Motorised Brigade at the time before being resubordinated via this order to the 1st Military District, was subordinated to the cabinet of the federal secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The purpose of this assignment be to make sure that the brigade command, the guards brigade command was doing their job properly? Would that be the purpose?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of any control in essence has that meaning, but it also has a wider context to be looked at; to monitor the situation on the ground, to provide assistance, and to personally see what the problems are; to communicate with the superior command so that issues could be dealt with more efficiently and quickly. I believe the authority of the cabinet of the federal secretary was such to provide a basis to deal with a lot of issues that the Guards Motorised Brigade or the Operations Group South may have had during the operation. Whether, indeed, this was so on the ground, that is something that can be discussed later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Colonel Pavkovic and Colonel Terzic be engaged with the Guards Motorised Brigade command, did that imply that either Pavkovic or Terzic --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- had any command responsibilities within the Guards Motorised Brigade or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did that also apply to the command of Operational Group South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Subsequently --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The authority of command, neither of them had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Subsequently were Commander Pavkovic and Terzic present in -- in Vukovar with the command of Operational Group South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry, that was my mistake, I meant Colonel Pavkovic and Terzic. And what were the functions of Colonel Pavkovic in Vukovar? What did he do?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what tasks he may have been given by his superior. As far as I know from my commander, Colonel Mrksic, he never used to receive any tasks. He monitored and specifically what I can tell you is that most of the time he was in the area of combat activities in the town of Vukovar, basically every day with the commanders of assault detachments. He monitored the situation and as to whether he always reported the situation to commander Colonel Mrksic, that I don't know. I would suppose so. But he was there most of the time in the field. While Colonel Terzic was not in the field, he was constantly at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to me that we can see in the transcript what the witness said, and that is that Colonel Pavkovic seldom informed or reported to Colonel Mrksic. Perhaps this can be clarified by my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What -- what needs to be clarified, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in answering one of the questions the witness said that Colonel Pavkovic occasionally informed Colonel Mrksic that he was mostly in the field, but that the actual reporting was quite seldom, appeared seldom. I don't find that in the transcript on page 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying some words were omitted? I'm sorry. I hadn't gathered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps I can clarify with the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you stated that Colonel Pavkovic never received any tasks from Colonel Mrksic and that most of the time he was in the field and that he monitored the situation and it's not clear whether or not he reported or he gave information to Mrksic often or -- or seldom -- seldomly. Can you please explain how often you believe Pavkovic informed Mrksic as to the situation in the field?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, very seldomly. Exceptionally seldomly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In any event, you spent most of your time in the headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that exhibit, Your Honour. It's Exhibit Number -- 65 ter number 453.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 404, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can look at tab 11, please, 65 ter number 454. It is a document dated the 1st of October, 1991, and it's entitled, "Order for blockade and attack." And it's signed and the author appears to be Mile Mrksic, the colonel.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: At this stage, the stage that the order was issued, the -- Colonel Mrksic was not the commander of Operational Group South, but the commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade as of the 1st of October; is that correct? 24

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't commander of Operations Group South, but rather the commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the document discusses tasks to be undertaken by the Guards Motorised Brigade, but I'd like to refer you to paragraph 2 of the order.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can briefly read out the first four or five lines of paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Guards Motorised Brigade will conduct a blockade and assault on Vukovar with the use of assault detachments within the operations group with the task in cooperation with Vukovar TO units (Petrova Gora detachment of the TO the armoured battalion of the 544th Motorised Brigade, break up enemy forces in the operations zone, take the town and establish an inspection regime." Is that enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and in relation to that statement were the TO, the Vukovar TO units and the Petrova Gora detachment, were they subordinated to the Guards Motorised Brigade at that stage or not? Because I see the word, "With the task in cooperation with these units." At this point in time, the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It concerns cooperation. The Guards Motorised Brigade at the time was not part, that is the Guards Motorised Brigade was then included within Operations Group South. And within the OG South there were the TO units of Petrova Gora, the armoured battalion of the 544th Motorised Brigade. That's why the command of the OG and its commander, Colonel Bojat, issued this; that's why it concerns coordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Petrova Gora TO, Territorial Defence, what was your understanding, what did that comprise of? About how many men?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I can't be precise as to the manning strength. Some of the documents were not at my disposal in the preparation for the testimony, and a lot of time has passed for me to be able to remember. Each detachment of the TO had about 100 to 150 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 150 to 200 men.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether the figures inside the TO Petrova Gora were such at the time, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what was it, generally?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. I know that the Petrova Gora detachment, once the Guards Motorised Brigade arrived to the area of Vukovar, was the only TO unit in the town of Vukovar of that level, of detachment level. There were some smaller units in the nearby villages, and in certain parts of the southern part of Vukovar, and they were at the level of company or platoon, when we came to Vukovar that particular TO detachment was commanded by Milorad Vujovic, and he remained in that position. He was subordinated to Colonel Bajo Bojat being the commander of the operations group. And he was trying to prevent the interference of the Croatian forces towards the barracks. That's all I know about the Petrova Gora TO unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that the commander of the TO detachment was Milorad Vujovic. Are you sure his first name is Milorad?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miroljub Vujovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was the ethnic make-up of this Petrova Gora detachment, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Also in the order, if we look further down, the tasks are being directed to assault detachments. And if we look at paragraph 5 it's entitled, "Unit tasks." And it has assault detachment 1 and explains the units or subunits that are incorporated into that assault detachment. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You explained yesterday what an assault detachment was. In this -- in this composition of assault detachment 1 it refers to the first battalion; is that correct? And other units. 1st Motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion of the guards brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion and the assault detachment number 1 was Major Borivoje Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And Captain Radic, do you know which assault detachment he was attached to, if any?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was within the assault detachment 1, and his commander was Major Borivoje Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document. It's 65 ter number 454.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will become Exhibit 405.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab number 12, please. It's 65 ter number 462. Now, this is a document dated the 12th of October, 1991. Could you briefly describe who that document --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- was to and who it was sent by?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was issued by the command of the 1st Military District, highly confidential, on the 12th of October. Deliver immediately, and the caution regards the system of command and control and order and discipline in the units. To the command of the 12th Corps, the 1st Proletarian Guards Division, and something that is illegible. I think it says Operations Group South, but the photocopy is quite poor. I suppose it was the Operations Group South, because we indeed received this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the command of the 12th Corps, the 1st Proletarian Guards Division, who did they belong to, what unit did they belong to? Were they in Operational Group South or some other unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can read from the document, this was a document issued by the command of the 1st Military District. The 12th Corps was under their command, as well as the guards motorised division, and the guards brigade, pursuant the previous decision by the chief of the general staff. And this is as late as the 12th of October, that means the Operations Group South was included as well. And all the units in the area were under the command of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The 12th Corps, were they attached to any operational group?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th Corps is a larger, higher ranking unit than the operations group. It was one of the strongest units inside the 1st Military District; it cannot be subordinated to an operational group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the caution pertains to all the units. The examples stated, as far as I know, do not concern the guards brigade. This was an issue that the command of the guards brigade dealt with quite efficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if we read the -- if you can read the first paragraph of the order, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the caution, item one: "There are units which are mixed and disorganised, from various organic compositions, in the areas where combat activities are carried out. The full resubordination was not carried out, the established system of command and answerability for the resubordinated units /is lacking/. Larger groups can be found wandering the other areas, /illegible/ the residents and organs of authority."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that the purpose of this order was to ensure that all units within the Operational Group South Command and the command of the 12th Corps were subordinated under one command? Is that the purpose of the order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. All units and those subordinated pursuant to orders, should be included in the formation and should be under full command of their superior commander. I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think you explained earlier, but were there any such problems in the area or the zone of responsibility of Operational Group South of soldiers appearing to be not under clear command? At that stage, the 12th of October.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said a minute ago, within Operations Group South there were no such instances. This issue had been dealt with previously, efficiently, and the entire area of responsibility was under the control of the military police units. We formed check-points on all roads in and out of the settlements within the combat area, and nothing could -- of this nature could take place, nothing as regards the issues discussed in this caution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When were these check-points set up in and out of the settlements? This is the 12th of October. Were they set up sometime earlier or just as of that date?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately upon our arrival to Vukovar and the command post at Negoslavci had to be secured based on the principles that were in use at the time, it was secured completely, including the entire territory. We were inspecting the territory and for that we used the first police battalion that was given the task, and that can be seen from the decisions by the commander. Therefore, that had been dealt with from the start.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then when you say the entire territory was secured, are you -- are you referring to the territory, the zone of responsibility of Operational Group South or some other area?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the area of responsibility of Operations Group South.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... used in paragraph 3, and if I perhaps read, it states, "I hereby order that you ensure the full re-subordination and answerability of the command structures for the subordinated and attached units." Can you explain what your understanding is of the term, the "full" subordination, of command structures and the attached units. What does the term, "full," mean, relating to Vukovar at the time or Operational Group South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had there been no problems relating to the procedure of resubordination, then it shouldn't have had this in the first place. I assume that there were cases in accordance with the order of the superior command in certain units. When full responsibility by the superiors was not carried out to place them under full command and in accordance with the lines of subordination, but from practice I know that it's not only the commanders that are responsible for such a situation. Well, actually, they are always responsible, but there were difficulties created for them that had to do with the dissatisfaction and lack of motivation amongst units who were from one unit resubordinated to another. There was even such a feeling amongst the officers themselves. So this was an attempt to emphasise the responsibility of senior officers for the resubordination of these units, particularly in case of volunteer units. There were a lot of problems in that case to place them under the command of the JNA. I wasn't as specific, perhaps, as required, but that's all that I needed to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... as of the 12th of October, what types of groups were expected to be subordinated? And I'm referring to, say, the other JNA units, Territorial Defence units, and volunteers.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an entry from the war diary regarding Operations Group South, detachment of the Kragujevac Territorial Defence came on the 8th of October, it was immediately placed under command, the commander of Lieutenant-Colonel Milo Dinov [phoen], there were no problems. On the 13th of October, the sabotage unit of the 93rd Protection Regiment, Major Stupar assigned by the commander in quite a precise way, no problems on the 9th and the 10th, the 3rd armoured battalion of the 211th Brigade resubordinated, tasked, assigned an area of responsibility, no problem. The 20th Partisan Brigade from Pozarevac on the 14th of October arrived in an organised fashion, took up the region brigade commander, accepted his assignment from commander Mrksic, no problems there. And then when the 80th and these other TOs came, it was the same situation. There were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and certainly by the 12th of October, 1991, were all armed units no matter what type, were the volunteers, TO, or other JNA units not in the Guards Motorised Brigade that were present in Operational Group South zone of responsibility, were they expected by this order to be under the full command of the command of Operational Group South? Is that the substance of the order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The substance of the order is to implement full resubordination, which units was regulated bit commander of the 1st Military District in the order, and it proceeded more or less as was noted in the war diary. As each unit arrived that's how this was regulated in terms of full command. The resubordinated unit was tasked and was treated as an organisational formation unit. That was the essence of all later cautions. All units that were resubordinated were to be treated as if they were organisational formational units, because it always would happen that some questions were not fully treated the question of standard, food, other issues relating to the units. However, these units in this case all received specific assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... particular order, are you able to say whether Colonel Mrksic implemented it, from your observations?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document, 65 ter number 931.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 406, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can look at tab number 14, please, and this is a document dated the 15th of October, 1991. And it's an order from the 1st Military District to Operational Group South and others. The Operational Group South command and others. Do you see this order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can read out paragraph 1 of that order, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Establish full control in the area of responsibility of the units. Pay special attention to the functioning of the military authority in all the settlements and do not permit the local organs of authority to interfere and exert influence, until the civilian control of the liberated territory is established."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and what is your understanding of what was being ordered there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was customary in the area where combat operations were underway to place everything under military command. In this case, as I see here, there is a request to pay attention to the functioning of the authorities in all the settlements and not to permit any kind of influence or interference by the local organs of authority. A JNA unit, once it enters an area or a zone, the host there would be the president of the local commune, the president of the municipality, and unless you dress him in a uniform and place a rifle on his back, it is very difficult for him to adapt to the situation and to accept that this was an area of combat operations, that it was war, and that he too is expected to participate. So from experience I know that all of those local authority organs, not that they were obstructing the work, but they were not actually offering any assistance. So naturally, according to the principles, everything was being placed under military authority, so they were supposed to be placed under military authority too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So this was an order to establish full military control over the area of Operational Group South's zone of responsibility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But not only in the area, this was an order for all commands that were subordinated to the 1st Military District, and also it refers to the Operations Group South.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of the order it refers to paramilitary compositions and volunteers which refused to put themselves under the command of the JNA are to be removed from the territory. Are you aware of any problems in Operational Group South's zone of responsibility as to volunteers not placing themselves under the command of Operational Group South? Or other units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes, there were, but it wasn't a wide-spread thing. There was an order by the commander to subordinate commanders in this sense, and that later the situation improved. So later there was no need to have those units removed. But there were problems, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were emphatic reactions on a number of occasions, but these units were not ultimately removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what -- what were those problems and when did they -- when did they start and how long did they go on for?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each volunteer unit, by the logic of the thing, once it entered an area of combat operations, would try to have autonomy, to command itself, and do whatever it wanted to. All of the volunteer units did not have any idea in advance of what the JNA was and what discipline meant in the guards brigade. So when they were placed under the command of a commander, for example, a company commander, and were told how they were supposed to act, then they would start to object, you would get questions, dissatisfaction and so on and so forth. But it would sometimes lead to the question being asked of whether they should be returned to where they came from and removed from the territory. Let me tell you right away, these units were formally under the control of the JNA. Regardless of how strict this command was, but as far as the -- the guards brigade I assert that the command was pretty strict. Still it was not possible to achieve any kind of effective command over these units. In some tasks they were quite efficient, they carried them out, but it is my impression that they also obstructed a lot of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the operational group -- sorry, what was the responsibility of the operational group commander, Operational Group South commander, in relation to volunteers that did not want to place themselves under the command, under his command?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this, it was his responsibility to remove them, but as I said, I remember that there were some problems, they were not pronounced problems, and as far as I can remember no unit was removed. But he was supposed to, under this order, to remove them. But I think that these matters were regulated in the Operations Group South with an oral and a written order, and I don't think that there were any problems there. Had there been any problems, there would be another written document in which the commander of the brigade would order that such and such a unit be removed in the area of responsibility. But, since there is no such entry in the war diary either, I don't think that there was such a document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In the order it states that commanders must make sure that the destruction of the damage of religious, cultural, and historical facilities in the liberated areas doesn't occur. Were there any such problems in the Operational Group South zone of responsibility of these facilities being destroyed?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really have no reliable information as to whether this happened or not. I didn't see any report, nor did I hear from anyone that this kind of thing happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document. It's Exhibit 461, 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 407, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can look at tab number 15, please, and it's 65 ter number 463. Do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And are you familiar it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In fact, on this document, and others, is it the case that you, in fact, drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I drafted the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how can you tell that you drafted the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the initials in the left corner of the document, "drafted by Major R. Trifunovic, typed by warrant officer 2nd Class D. Ristovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... directed to.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the author is concerned, I explained yesterday how this decision was made. The commander, together with the organs of the command by applying any of the methods of work of the command in adopting decisions. And it was sent to the assault detachment 1, assault detachment 2, assault detachment 3, assault detachment 4, the Partisan Brigade TO, the 2nd TO in Sremska Mitrovica, the 3rd Battalion of the Armoured Brigade, the Armoured Brigade of the Guards Brigade, the Sabotage Detachment of the Protective Brigade, the 1st Battalion of the Military Police. LSAT PVO Deputy Commander for logistics, the commander of the Engineers Company, and the original document to the operations and training organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm speaking a little bit fast, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, this was a -- an order by Colonel Mrksic on the 15th of October, 1991. And it states "to continue the assault operations on Vukovar"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can look at paragraph 2, where it says unit tasks, it refers to assault detachment 1 and it states what units assault detachment 1 comprised of. And one of those units it states is a volunteers company from the current combat deployment. Do you know who that volunteers company was that was subordinated to assault detachment 1?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really say, but there are only two possibilities. One is that this was a company from the immediate sector, actually from any of the villages in the operations zone, because sometime in mid-October there was an order to carry out a mobilisation of the local population. In order to bring the forces up to par on the front lines. So mobilisation was carried out in Negoslavci, in the village of Berak, in all of the villages in the zone of operations. That's one possibility. The other possibility is that that was one of the companies of volunteers that were arriving from different parts or different towns such as Sabac, Stara Pazova, Smederevska Palanka, Sremska Mitrovica, and so on. I am talking about possibilities, but I don't know exactly which company it was I see that it is also mentioned there in the 2nd Assault Detachment, so this is what the possibilities are, either they were from the broader area or from the immediate area of the zone of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you aware of a volunteers unit with the name Leva Supoderica operating in the zone of responsibility of Operational Group South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was that -- was that unit subordinate to the command of Operational Group South?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a very broad sense. It was subordinated to the commander of assault group 1, and by virtue of that fact, to the commander of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will break now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, earlier I tendered 65 ter number 931, that was a mistake. It should be 65 ter number 462, and that relates to Exhibit 406. Document number 13, which is 931, hasn't been dealt with yet, but will be later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, before the break we were talking about the order from Colonel Mrksic to continue assault operations on the 15th of October, 1991. And we spoke about the units that are attached to assault detachment 1. And then you stated in answer that the Leva Supoderica unit was subordinated to the commander of assault group 1. When you say assault group 1, are you referring to assault detachment 1 or in fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think the witness mentioned the assault group. I think he said this was subordinated to assault detachment 1, and I think we've got this distinction clarified already. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, from the transcript at page 30, line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I recall both being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: At line 20 it's recorded --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's not clear in my mind yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Just to clarify, Witness, you stated that at some point in time the Leva Supoderica unit was attached to -- well, who was it attached to? Assault detachment 1 or assault group 1? Can you clarify?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assault detachment 1. I don't know whether I've actually mentioned the assault group. I may have misspoken, but I don't think we've got that far yet. Assault detachment number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And we'll look at further documents relating to that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document, which is number 463.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will become Exhibit 408.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we look at tab number 16, please. This is a document that's dated the 19th of October, 1991 from the 1st Military District command, and it's addressed to a number of compositions, one being Operational Group South. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In the document it refers to, after subparagraph 2, the words -- refers to a term called, "Ustasha." "The probable intentions of the Ustasha authorities in Croatia are to" -- and then it goes on to explain what the intentions of that group was. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What does the term, "Ustasha" mean, what do you believe that term to mean in the context of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term Ustasha is a term already encountered in the orders and decisions of the superior command. The ones that we have already seen. I'm not qualified to explain why this term was introduced here. There must have been a logic behind this, something along the lines of all the Croats who did not oppose the JNA were not Ustashas, and those who were opposing the JNA were Ustashas. But this wasn't a term made up by someone from Operations Group South. It must have been someone from the superior command, rather. What the reason was for that, I really have no clue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that, and can you explain what the historical connotation of the term Ustasha is?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The historical connotation dates back to World War II when some of the Croatian forces, or rather some of the Croatian people joined the axis powers. And those Croats committed crimes in areas populated by Serbs. I'm no expert myself, I think they actually called themselves Ustashas, Ante Pavlic, and those people. However, as far as I remember, I was still young, and we were taught at school that these people were members of some Croatian units who fought with the Germans, and these units committed crimes against the Serbian population, especially in areas belonging to the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. The order refers to a number of things, but particularly it refers to strict measures to be taken against undisciplined behaviour. And if we look at paragraph 3 of the order, the -- it discusses a situation where some troops consumed large amounts of alcohol and as a result of that a warning is issued that it may lead to serious incidents. Do you see that, that part of the document, the order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I apologise. Number 3. I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 4 it orders the addressees or the commands of the various zones of responsibility to take out measures. Can you read out paragraph 4, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In order to prevent looting, the abuse of citizens and murder, even that of prisoners, all armed persons and groups which are not part of the JNA or the TO, Chetniks and such, shall be disarmed and taken in. Their leaders shall be incarcerated and legal steps shall be taken against them."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: At that point in time, and we're talking about the 19th of October now, are you aware of any incidents of looting and murder of citizens or prisoners in Operational Group South's zone of responsibility, bearing in mind that this order came from the command of the military district?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of any such incidents within Operations Group South at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: As a result of this order from the 1st Military District, are you aware whether there were any follow on orders from Colonel Mrksic to the subordinated units in his zone of responsibility, Operational Group South to implement the higher order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be specific, but I believe that the work of Operations Group South with regard to all these issues was responsible, which would lead me to assume that an order was actually written down, or alternatively that the commander informed the commanders and the brigade command about these problems at a briefing. If there was nothing in writing, then I'm certain this was at least noted down in their own working notebooks. I am certain that this order was complied with as far as these aspects are concerned. Apart from everything else, these are the sort of measures that had been known to have been applied before in order to prevent murder and looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document, and it's 65 ter number 464.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 409, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab number 17, please. And this is 65 ter number 5. This is a document dated the 29th of October, 1991. And it's a decision of Colonel Mrksic, Operational Group South commander, for the continuation of assault of the operation in Vukovar. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph 2, it issues an order to the Assault Detachment 1, and within that it states that the Leva Supoderica unit, or detachment, is part of Assault Detachment 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know the composition of the Leva Supoderica detachment, who those men were, and how many?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were from the Leva or Desna Supoderica, from those areas. Those were TO men. And some were members of the radical party who arrived as volunteers in the operations area under Operations Group South, roughly at this time meaning between the 15th and 20th of October, and onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know who the commander of that detachment was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Leva Supoderica, you mean? Commander Lancuzanin, also known as Kameni.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that some were members of the radical party. Which radical party are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The radical party. The radical party. It had branches throughout this area, in Serbia, in Eastern Slavonia, as well as in other republics of the SFRY at the time. I don't know which particular branch this happened to be. They may have arrived from Serbia or maybe they were just locals. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who was the head of this radical party, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically for this detachment, you mean? The radical party, as a political party, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, the radical party.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In Assault Detachment 1 it refers to the Petrova Gora TO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: From that do we conclude that the Petrova Gora TO was attached to -- was subordinated to Assault Detachment 1?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that document, Your Honour. It's 65 per number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 410, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab number 18, please. This is 65 ter number 583. This is an order from Colonel Mrksic dated the 9th of November. The translation has an incorrect year, but 1991 in the original. And the number, military number is 349-1.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In the order he -- Colonel Mrksic orders that a command be formed in Negoslavci village with Major Vukasinovic as a locality commander, and Captain Bozic as a Deputy Commander. Major Vukasinovic and Captain Bozic, what units did they belong to, what specific units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Ljubisa Vukasinovic was a member of the brigade command. He was attached to the security organ. He was not with the unit, he was with the brigade command. I think he was the most senior administrator in the security organ. Since he was a member of the command, it was only logical for a man attached to the command, even more so since he was a security officer, to be the commander of the place where the command was physically located. Mile Bozic was Deputy Commander of the 1st Battalion of the military police and Sretko Jankovic was at the time. As for these other commands, their commanders were assigned in keeping with the principle of command responsibility prevailing in their respective areas. The commanders within the area of combat operations around Vukovar were all assigned based on their respective responsibilities in terms of each of the operations areas within the town itself. This order is a direct result from another order from the superior command, and was the result of a need to have these matters sorted out. There was the previous order from the military district command demanding that military authorities be established on account of the problems encountered in the work of the civil authorities and because some of the military actions that had been taken had been hampered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we look at paragraph -- if we look at paragraph 4 it states that, "I appoint as commanders for Vukovar town the commanders of the assault detachments for the part of the town within their operations zones."

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is very specific, regardless of how it looks. The operations area is the same thing as the area of responsibility, when we talk about the actual functioning of military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in this order he also orders that commands be set up in Berak village and also in Ovcara, and Jakubovac village and Grabovo village sectors.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Commanders of some parts of an area, and the commander of one part of the sector was Colonel Slobodan Misovic; he was the commander. He was in charge of this whole area, and he was the appointed commander. And these here are commanders, deputy commanders for all the brigades under him. And these people were in charge of the sectors surrounding Ovcara, Jakubovac, and Glogovac. They were appointed commanders of these respective areas. Whether the commander of the partisan brigade was Mis [phoen] or Slobodan, but that seems to be in relation to all these three villages and maybe to the entire sector because there was another hamlet there, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was your understanding for the reason for setting up smaller commands or subdividing some areas of Operational Group South into smaller subordinate commands? What's the purpose of this order? Why was this done, if you know.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand this, at least not the way you phrased the question. Each commander is responsible for his own area, the one that was assigned to him within the operations area, for his own sector. However, in purely practical terms it was sometimes the case that his responsibility boiled down to merely carrying out combat operations. In settled areas, for example, in Negoslavci, the local authorities would sometimes act unsupervised. Obviously there were -- had to be a curfew, movement would have had to be restricted. Able-bodied men who could have been involved in the fighting should have been placed under his command, only the commander could have done this. The local commander, if he had been authorised to do so, but there are certain rules, the rules of service, and of our rules, which state precisely what the tasks are and the duties of a local commander, so that it doesn't boil down to the responsibility of carrying out combat operations within his own sector. He had to have full authority over all the other issues: Order, discipline, food, the local population, the prisoners, the wounded and everything else that the situation entailed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So in summary --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I apologise to my learned friend, but I think there is something in the transcript, a possible misinterpretation on page 39, and the line number is 20. It says here that only the commander can do this, and I think the witness actually said the local commander. So that's a difference. The witness was talking about the local commander, and I believe it might be a good idea for my learned friend to have this clarified. The English transcript only says commander and not local commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the problem may be in the punctuation. If you ignore the full stop, the witness is saying this could have been placed under his command, only the commander could have done this, the local commander, if he had been authorised to do so, but there are certain rules, et cetera. I think it's clear enough that the witness made it clear that he was speaking of the local commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, does this mean that this was an order enforcing complete military authority over any civilian authority that may have existed in any of those areas?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The town commanders or village commanders that are referred to in this order, who are they subordinate to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are subordinate to whoever appointed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, Commander Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we look at further down the order, it also instructs that there should be prevention of any ill treatment of the population and local inhabitants and unauthorised entry and searches of apartments and houses. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: As of the 9th of November were you aware whether or not, in fact, that was occurring in Operational Group South's zone of responsibility, and in particular, these areas, or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such incidents, but to a lesser extent. However, unless military authority had been established and an appropriate system of command, it might have been the case that looting occurred among the local population, neighbour to neighbour, so to speak. But it could have been a military civilian. So it was only logical for these issues to be dealt with like this. So if Misovic was the commander, he had to take appropriate measures such as the ones outlined in the order of the commander of Operations Group South. You know what locals are like, they go from one place to another to fetch something, to give somebody grief over there just because at some point in time a long time ago they had harmed them in some way or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I know it's speculation on your part, but you said that it could have been a military civilian that was involved in the looting. Is that a mistranslation? It's either a military person or a civilian person; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military or civilian, everybody was susceptible to sanctions, potentially imposed by the local commander. Whenever it came to issues like unauthorised entry, ill-treatment e searching houses, only the local command he would have been in a position to get this sort of thing under control and to mete out appropriate punishment, and he himself would have been responsible to the commander of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender document 583, Your Honour. That is the last document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, to the registry record this document was already admitted -- tendered and admitted on the 27th of April, 2006, as Exhibit 374.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab 19, please, which is 65 ter Exhibit Number 956. It's a document dated the 14th of November, 1991, with confidential number 394-2. And it's an order from Colonel Mrksic regulating the issue of the control of the territory and the support unit. Do you see that document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph number 5, Colonel Mrksic orders further that full control be established in relation to movement in and out of the settlements, identification of persons who wish to remove into a settlement and immediate arrest of all suspects, interview them, and based on the gathering of information, react decisively. Now, who is this order directed to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commanders and commanding officers of the units there as well as the local commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So, in fact, is that all subordinate commanders in the operational group zone of responsibility? Because it doesn't specify particularly.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was issued by the commander of the Operations Group South. That means that it includes all commanders within the Operations Group South, and it also concerns itself with local commanders or commanders or particular settlements. That means the order encompassed all commanders within the area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document, Your Honour. It's Exhibit 956 -- sorry, 65 ter 956.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 411, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab number 20, please, 65 ter number 4. It's a document dated the 15th of November, 1991 at 2000 hours. The number is 405-1, the military number, and it's an order for resubordination by Colonel Mrksic. Do you have that order in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what is the effect of that order, the effect of that resubordination order? What is he asking or ordering to occur?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order is clear that the Territorial Defence detachment of Stara Pazova is to be resubordinated to the 80th motorised Brigade and that all subordination issues will be regulated by the commander of the 80th Motorised Brigade. As to why he decided to resubordinate the Stara Pazova detachment to the 80th Brigade, I don't know. Perhaps there was a task envisaged for the 80th Brigade to be carried out. I apologise, it had already been given a task defined by the decision of the 14th of November, and the correction of the decision of the 15th of November. Therefore, I believe there was a need to reinforce, to strengthen the unit, and so he decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the 80th Motorised Brigade, based on this order, on the 15th of November, 1991, who was that brigade subordinate to, based on this order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to this order, the 80th Motorised Brigade was within Operations Group South, and it was resubordinated to OG South by a previous order by the commander of the 1st Military District. I believe that took place on the 7th of November. By that order it was resubordinated to OG South, at that time the 7th or the 8th, and it had been given a task inside the zone of operations. As to what the task was, I can't say, but the commander decided to resubordinate the Stara Pazova TO detachment to the brigade to improve efficiency in carrying out the assigned task, so I believe. He had his reasons. Therefore, it fell under OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document, Your Honour. It's 65 ter number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit Number 412, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab number 21, please. This is 65 ter number 601. And it's an order from the 1st Military District command signed by Zivota Panic, lieutenant general, and it's an order to a number of commands, including Operation Group South. And this order relates to the resubordination of units within these commands' areas of responsibility, the effect of resubordination of them. If you can read paragraph 1 of the order, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Through or by inspecting the implementation of my orders I personally ascertained that certain tasks had not been carried out or they were carried out superficially.
