The resubordinated units were taken -- took insufficient care, the unit commands were not informed on the situation in the territory, and on the results achieved. The tasks weren't handed down to detachment commanders, or they are given little time to forward the tasks to their subordinates. The establishment of the military authority and the settlement commands establishment was not being carried out completely. In order to overcome these shortcomings, I hereby order."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we look at, say, paragraph 2, the first sentence of paragraph 2, can you read that sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Immediately start establishing military authorities and the town commands in the liberated territories and settlements. The military authority in town commands" --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can read paragraph well -- sorry, paragraph 1 which explains in more detail what the 1st Military District command ordered these other commands to do.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Admit the directly subordinated and attached units with full responsibility and treat them as establishment composition until a task is carried out. Apply the same treatment to the attached and resubordinated units of the JNA, the TO and the volunteer units, provided they are put under the command of the JNA, regardless of whether they are to be engaged in the carrying out of combat tasks, to control the territory or in order to establish military authority. Pay particular care to the logistical support of the attached and resubordinated units. Commanders mentioned here, inter alia the commander of OG South are answerable to me for the execution of this task."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to pay particular care in relation to that, to where he states that particular care should be taken to the logistical support to the attached and resubordinated units, would this also refer to the TO units and the Leva Supoderica unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order by the 1st Military District command, and it specifies here that particular care should be given to logistic support. The logistics support for the Operations Group South was quite well-organised. And all the establishment units were included, as well as those that were attached and volunteers' units, as well as TO units. The entire system functioned adequately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what type of logistical support would that be? What types -- what types of support, in practical terms?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to be as precise, although one can offer various definitions. The function or the task of the rear battalion is to supply ammunition, fuel, materiel, parts, including maintenance of the aforementioned. Then to supply food, equipment, and I mean uniforms, medication and medical issues in general, to regulate the traffic, and some additional tasks assigned to logistics, including, on occasion, construction. Those would be the basic functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Would that include ammunition as well, and weapons?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The supply of weapons and ammunition, I have already mentioned that, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what is your understanding as to why this particular order was issued? Probably clear from the order, but just in brief terms, why was this issued from the 1st Military District at this time?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can base my assumption on the date here, and I conclude that in spite of the warning issued previously, the practice or the situation continued in terms of inadequate reception of units and inadequate accommodation and work conditions for those units that have arrived. This focuses particularly on logistics, because it was a sensitive issue. If a unit is resubordinated and if they are not received the way they should, there is dissatisfaction, poor morale, lack of motivation, the wish to return. That's what took place in the armed forces, including the JNA units. And I believe within the command of -- the operations group had been dealt with completely, and that at the time there was no dissatisfaction that could concern this particular order on the 16th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And there you are referring to the zone of responsibility of Operations Group South; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The area of responsibility of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And within this order there is a warning given in paragraph 3 as to if this full control isn't -- isn't met or attained, and can you read out paragraph 3, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I strongly forbid that the liberated or captured territory be deserted or left outside of the control of the units of the JNA or the TO. The commanding officers who fail to comply with this task are to be put under the most severe disciplinary measures."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document. It's 65 ter number 601.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 413, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab number 22, please. This is 65 ter number 932. It's a document dated the 16th of November, 1991 at 6.00. The military number is 407-1. It's a combat report signed by Colonel Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And it's a report that's being sent to the 1st Military District command and the Federal Secretariat for National Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In the document it relates to an issue of the problem of motivation of certain elements of the volunteer units and the TO members, with regards to the participation in the combat, are still present. Do you see that, it's in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What was your understanding of that problem at that time? Are you aware of that problem, with motivation of some of the TO and the volunteer-unit members to participate?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you explain a little what that problem was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problems that affected motivation. The first one was the general exhaustion of the units by being deployed for extensive periods of time in the combat zone in Vukovar. Some units had spent as many as 45 days there. If we are to bear in mind that the guards brigade was replenished by additional troops and including the troops that had already been at the barracks, the time spent in Vukovar extended up to two months. There was constant combat activity inside the town and people were under a lot of stress due to unexpected events that could occur day and night. It all affected the troops negatively, although on occasion there were rotations during cease-fire periods that were regulated by some higher echelons. That was the first reason for poor motivation. The second one was that it didn't seem to -- it didn't seem that it will end any time soon. Everyone thought that the whole thing would last far shorter. There were also problems that were regulated by the Federal Secretariat as concerns reservists. They stipulated that it can spend only 45 to 60 days in their respective units and their dead-lines were about to run out. The people kept asking how long or how much more they were to stay. There were no guarantees provided and no dead-lines set for their return. There were also regular conscripts there of Serb or Croatian ethnicity who had already been sent home after having served their military term, who were supposed to have been sent home. And all these reasons, plus the military situation resulted in all the problems pertaining to poor motivation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: At that point in time, the 16th of November, this -- your understanding of this report is that Colonel Mrksic is reporting on lack of motivation as opposed to lack of discipline in this report?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the lack of motivation. I don't know whether you saw where it's mentioned here that these problems have been persistent as of the 4th of November when the dead-lines were set for the conscripts to be sent home, for the reservists to be relieved as well, and the entire operation wasn't going the way it was planned. And that's when they began feeling this lack of motivation problem and the brigade command was well aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document, it's 900 -- 65 ter number 932.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 414, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab number 24 - we've dealt with tab number 23 - and this is 65 ter number 444. It's a document dated the 18th of November, 1991. It's from the 1st Military District command signed by Lieutenant-General Panic. And it's an order directed to, amongst others, Operational Group South. In paragraph 1 of that order, I would ask you to read that paragraph out, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I hereby order: 1. OG South carry out detailed and complete preparations and in coordinated action with tactical group north; take the hospital and the Ministry of the Interior building and mop up the remaining Ustasha forces in the liberated part of the town on the morning of the 19th of November, 1991, by 1000 hours. Continue to clear up Mitnica and downtown Vukovar until it is completely safe and secure to move around the town." I've concluded with item 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. So it's an order to take the hospital. Which hospital was that referring to, or what's your understanding of which hospital that is?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The town hospital of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if we look at paragraph 3, if you can read that out, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "While carrying out these assignments and in all other operations in the area in which the units of the 1st Military District are engaged on smashing Ustasha forces, observe all aspects of the Geneva on smashing Ustasha forces, observe all aspects of the Geneva Conventions on the prisoners of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to that order that the Geneva Conventions on the prisoners of war be respected, do you know whether any follow-up on orders in writing was sent to the subordinates -- subordinate units in Operational Group South's command?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. I don't think it was on the 18th. I don't think it was written on the 18th, but on the 19th, and I have in mind a written document regulating the evacuation from the hospital. I don't seem to remember whether it was written on the 18th or the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll look at that document later. But if we can move to paragraph 5, it's further ordered that the behaviour of soldiers in the carrying out of these activities should be appropriate. And if you can read the paragraph 5 out, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All units are to carry out comprehensive and thorough preparations for combat against Ustasha forces, and commanders at all levels will be responsible for this. During preparations, on the 19th of November, 1991, most resolutely prevent any disobedience, unsoldierly appearance and behaviour. Commanders at all levels will ensure realistic and favourable conditions for this task to be published. All officers and soldiers who fail to follow this order shall pay a fine of up to 20 per cent of their salaries. Inform all soldiers and officers of this. "To ensure the requested soldierly appearance and behaviour, repeat relevant basic military skills and procedures."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can stop you there. And this duty or responsibility has been further expanded upon in paragraph 8, to ensure that the operations are carried out correctly. And if you can read paragraph 8 out, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Every unit must fully control the situation on the territory in its area of responsibility. Commanders at all levels will be responsible for this. Wartime laws have not entered into force and therefore - as always - nobody has the right to retribution and other kinds of revenge, which some local TO units carried out. In future, arrest those who commit any such acts and undertake appropriate legal measures."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And further in paragraph 9, the order relates to ensuring that volunteers, et cetera, are placed under the command of the JNA in these combat operations. Can you read that paragraph out, then I'll ask you some questions about it, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All units and formations (volunteers, local communes, et cetera) participating in combat operations in the territory of the 1st Military District must be under the command of the JNA or else they will be disarmed and taken away while extremists will be arrested and appropriate legal measures will be undertaken."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In ordering these operations and the taking of the Vukovar Hospital, do you think it was reasonable that all of these warnings in relation to how soldiers were to behave in these operations and do you think it was reasonable that they were placed in this order as a commander, from your experience?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these things had to be noted. The regulations that we discussed yesterday define all of these matters, who is being resubordinated, how they're being resubordinated, what would be the relationships and who is responsible for what. In the specific case, and in order to prevent problems and failings in practice, this is quite understandable and normal. It's justified to write something like this, especially in accordance with the principle that the command monitors the situation and reacts on the basis of received reports in order to direct everyone towards the objective, and the objective is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to this document on the 18th of November, 1991, it states that the Croatian armed forces are defeated in the area of combat operations carried out by the 1st Military District units. It then states, "However, the war did not end with the fall of Vukovar, and an even more fearsome and brutal war against Ustasha forces is now ahead of us." Do you agree that at the time that this order was written that Vukovar, in terms of the town, had fallen, to the -- to the JNA and other armed forces under Operational Group South's zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The town was practically -- well, not in the hands of, but it was captured on the 18th and control was established in the town by Operations Group South. What is mentioned about the war continuing, I think that all that came later, such as possibilities of sabotage, blockades and subsequent resistance, these were things that had to be warned about. But as far as the objective of going through the front lines and everything in those terms, the operation was concluded. Once the operation was concluded though some other problems cropped up and then the commander was obliged to deal with those problems in the proper way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Lieutenant-General Panic envisaged that -- in this order that there may be a possibility that there might be retribution and kinds of revenge against captured prisoners or civilians. Do you think that was an unreasonable assumption on his part as a basis of this order, that revenge may, in fact, occur and the situation of captured prisoners, et cetera, in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe that it was reasonable, such a possibility did exist. Possibility of retribution, and one had to be aware of that possibility. So this kind of thinking is quite reasonable, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Had you heard of any acts of revenge or retribution in the area of Operational Group South, the zone of responsibility, prior to this order being issued on the 18th of November?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we're talking about the 18th, as far as I can recall, a part of the Croatian forces from the Mitnica had surrendered, and there were no serious incidents. A part of the forces had surrendered from the central sector of Vukovar, and there were no more serious incidents there either. Certain officers who were in contact and in the area of combat activities attended and observed this withdrawal and kept reporting to the commander. Other than small verbal provocations or mild physical assaults, there were no more serious incidents in the process, as far as I know, on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. However, in this order from the 1st Military District, which of course is a larger area than Operational Group South's zone of responsibility, it states that some local Territorial Defence units had carried out some acts of revenge. Do you see that? This is just about -- in paragraph 8, and then it states, "In future, arrest those who commit these acts."

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: My question is, do you know where these acts of revenge had been carried out, if not in Operational Group South's zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not in the area of responsibility of OG South. We're talking about local TO. So this refers to the settlements in that area. The OG South zone, other than the place where the command post was, and the village of Berevce [phoen] and this area around Jakubovac, all of that was the outlying area. The rest of the zone of responsibility encompassed the town itself. So the area of responsibility of OG South did not actually have any local units that could create such problems. Everything was under control in Negoslavci, in Berak, at Ovcara, and Jakubovac. On the 18th also everything was under control, the units were pulling out of Mitnica on the 18th, there were no problems there either. On the 18th there were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: However, in the town of Vukovar itself there were TO units and volunteer units attached to assault detachments, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: One last question on this topic. You said that it was reasonable that this warning was given in relation to guarding against acts of revenge by TO, TO personnel against civilians or prisoners that were captured, why in light of the situation in Vukovar, namely the town had fallen by the 18th of October -- or November, why do you think it was reasonable to issue this order in light of the situation that was developing? Or this warning, I mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a warning for everyone, not just for Vukovar. And it didn't relate just to the situation in Vukovar. If I were to answer your question now, you know when such a large town is liberated or large parts of a town of that size, and the members of the Territorial Defence who are from that town are present, and when someone is surrendering and the Croatian side was actually surrendering in different parts of the town and then later in some other locations, it's normal to expect some sort of a reaction, because one side shot the other, and the other -- and the other side shot them back. So it was to be expected that there were some -- there would be some problems or some incidents, and that's why it was natural to expect some problems like that to occur and to deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look at paragraph 9, please, if you can read that out. Paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All units and formations (volunteers, local units, and others) participating in combat operations in the territory of the 1st Military District must be under the command of the JNA or else they will be disarmed and taken away, while extremists will be arrested and appropriate legal measures will be undertaken."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: This order was addressed to, amongst other groups, Operational Group South command. Are you aware whether Colonel Mrksic had seen this order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he did see it. It's recorded in the log. I think that there's an entry also in the war diary. He should have been informed about all of the orders, either by somebody from the operations body or from the officer on duty or from the general administration office.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to my learned friend but I think that the witness said that the commander, Colonel Mrksic, wrote an order on the 18th or the 19th on the basis of this order. I don't remember precisely. So I think that the question as to whether Colonel Mrksic did or did not see this order is a leading one because how could he have written an order to OG South without having seen the order first, and the witness already answered this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I can only respond that I didn't say to the witness Colonel Mrksic saw it or he didn't see it, just simply is he aware whether he did see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's so, Mr. Vasic. And the answer is that the witness thought that he did, and it was recorded in the log. And perhaps the war diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document, it's 65 ter number 444.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will become Exhibit 415.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab 25, please. This is 65 ter number 575. And it's a warning submitted -- sent by the 1st Military District command with military number 1614-167. It's dated the 18th of November, 1991. And it's submitted to, it states, amongst others, the command of Operational Group South. If you can briefly read that order, then I'll ask you some questions about it, please. That warning.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Since the Ustasha forces are surrendering in Vukovar and Borovo while simultaneously citizens, women, children and old people are fleeing Vukovar and Borovo, in that respect and upon the request of the SSNO, Federal Secretariat for the National Defence, I hereby draw your attention to ensure fair treatment, maximum vigilance, and protection of our own units. In the course of the evening take measures to secure the units and individuals so as to prevent sabotage activities and unwanted accidents. When receiving the refugees, strictly adhere to instructions which were given earlier, and the detainees are to be secured with enough troops along with all the other necessary measures."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. This order is a more specific order, a warning, than the previous one in that the addressees are -- there's only two addressees on this one and the partisan guards motorised division and Operational Group South; is that correct? As well as the 12th Corps. Is that correct? It's a more specific -- there is a more specific addressee list?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That relate to the particular problems of the protection of citizens, women and children, in the Vukovar and Borovo area. At this time, on the 18th of November, were you aware of any detainees, any prisoners of war, whether they be civilians or combatants, being taken into the custody of Operational Group South units on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Already on the 18th at noon in the area of the town and the Mitnica area, there were already many civilians; women, children, the elderly. There were also the wounded there, as well as members of the Croatian forces with weapons who had surrendered. And that's when the decision was made, because the previous day assistance was requested by the 1st Military District in terms of transport, so already on that day, the 18th, they needed to be transported, these wounded, the population, women and children, the wounded, the elderly, i.e. the civilians. They wanted to leave. Those who had surrendered and who had carried weapons were to go to Sremska Mitrovica. As far as I can remember, there was an attempt on the 18th to transfer these people through Nustar and Sid via Vinkovci, whereas these other people who had been carrying weapons and who had surrendered who were soldiers were supposed to be taken to Sremska Mitrovica where they were supposed to be interrogated. As far as I can remember though, on the 18th there were a lot of problems primarily because the Croatian authorities did not want to receive the people who were being sent to Croatian territory, and I think that on the 18th even they came back and then there were many problems on the night of the 18th and 19th, how to care for these people, where to put them up, how to provide food for them, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: There was -- there is a later document that relates to that particular problem with the Croatian authorities, and we can talk about that then. But you state that on the night of the 18th and 19th there were many problems, how to care for these people, where to put them up. But my specific question is, to your knowledge were there any detention centres that were keeping these people, either prisoners of war or civilians in the town of Vukovar as of the 18th and 19th?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it means, this detention centre, that's not clear to me. There were places, certain buildings or facilities where people were assembled, and where a selection of the people was made. As far as I know, those locations were Velepromet, the barracks, in town, and the military farm at Ovcara. The farm at Ovcara, as far as that goes, I think that's -- that the people from Mitnica were there on the 18th. We're talking about the 18th, and they were transported. Whether after that when they were returned by the Croatian authorities as to whether they returned to the same location or if they were taken to some closer locations out of those three that I mentioned, that's something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Just in relation to the 18th, not any future date like the 19th or 20th, but as of the 18th do you know whether people were being detained in the area of Velepromet, the barracks or Ovcara or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that from Mitnica and apart from the town centre were assembled at those locations, assembled. Assembled and guarded. They could not have been detained because they were not arrested, they didn't stand trial or anything. They were gathered there and that the selection was supposed to have been carried out. So probably the selection was carried out then on the 19th. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in relation to this warning, are you aware whether Colonel Mrksic had received it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All warning, all orders, had to pass through the hands of the commander or the Chief of Staff. In what way? Either the administration office would place them on the desk of the commander or this would be done by the Chief of Staff or the chief of operations. The commander of OG South was informed about all important questions. He wasn't informed about minor problems, so it's understandable that he shouldn't be burdened with such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to the warning, it requests that the commanders adhere to instructions which were given earlier about receiving refugees; they ask them to strictly adhere to them. Had you seen those instructions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier instructions -- earlier warnings, are you talking about earlier warnings or earlier orders? Well, there were such things. We did receive several warnings before that from our superior command relating to taking care of the prisoners. It was just a question of how specific those warnings were so that we could act on them. You needed to be quite specific regarding such a serious matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And what -- I'm just reading off the document, it says "strictly adhere to instructions." What do you understand that to mean, what types of instructions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that those are the warnings that were sent that we talked about earlier, or perhaps some other ones that we don't have here with us right now, but there were such warnings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document, Exhibit Number -- sorry, 65 ter number 575.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will become Exhibit 416.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 25 seconds short of 12.30, so perhaps the time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab number 26, please. This document doesn't have a 65 ter number, so the ERN numbers are for the English, 0467-2867, to 0467-2868. And for the B/C/S 2467-2867 to 2467-2868. Witness, do you see that document in front of you? It's a document dated 1800 hours on the 18th of November?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It's a report from Colonel Mrksic to the 1st Military District. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in that report it summarises activities up until approximately that time, 6.00 in the afternoon on the 18th of November. Would you agree with that? Activities undertaken by Operational Group South units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In that report it's the Mitnica evacuation and the Mitnica surrender is -- it discussed as to what happened on that particular day in relation to that surrender. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the report is quite detailed as to how the surrender took place, the meetings that led to the surrender and what was being done to resolve that situation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in that -- in that report it states that activities on the sorting out through, and the transport of civilians and the Ustashas are going on. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document. It has no ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 417, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab 27, please. This again has no 65 ter number. The English ERN is 0467-2869 to 0467-2871 and the B/C/S is 0467-2869 to 0467-2871. Witness, this is a report to the 1st Military District command and the cabinet of the Federal Secretariat for the National Defence, it's dated the 19th of November at 1800 hours, and it's signed by Colonel Mrksic. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When we look at this document in this regular combat report, the last paragraph of paragraph 1 or of the last subparagraph, paragraph 1, it states, "According to the statements of a corporal and two soldiers who were in the Vukovar Hospital there are many of the hospital staff who are members of the HDZ and the Ustasha forces hiding and concealing themselves in various ways." Do you see that information?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how was that information obtained? Are you able to add anything further? How was that received at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once the hospital had been taken these three members of the army were set free. They were taken back to the command post at Negoslavci. I'm not sure if Dr. Vesna Bosanac was with them or whether she came before or even slightly later. But she was the hospital director and she was the one who had them released. I myself spoke to Sergeant Jovic, who said that throughout their time at the Vukovar Hospital in addition to the wounded civilians, women and elderly, there were people carrying arms taking shelter and hiding there. They started concealing themselves by putting on hospital overcoats in order to conceal their uniforms and pass themselves off at patients, that was at least was the soldiers reported. And that's accurate; I mean what is accurate is that they said this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who was -- were you at that meeting with Dr. Bosanac?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do know, how much, that Dr. Vesna Bosanac came to the command post. I didn't see her myself, I was in a room somewhere and she probably went straight to the commander's room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say the commander's room, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of Operations Group South, Colonel Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... paragraph 2 entitled, "Operational Group South units," it states that "during the day liberated areas mopped up and the civilians were being pulled from and evacuated from parts of Vukovar and there was work on sorting through the Ustasha forces from the central part of Vukovar." It further states, "The pulling out activities were hindered by big numbers of civilians and was the work -- and as was the work of provision of accommodation and security for them." Also states "this activity was also hindered by the fact that the Ustasha government refused to admit a big number of civilians sent to Zupanja yesterday, so they were subsequently sent back to us again." Do you know why the Croatians, the Croatian government refused these refugees?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that. I can only assume what one of the reasons might have been. They were hoping for an exchange, perhaps, at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we go further down the report, it states that, "At this moment Operational Group South units fully control all parts of Vukovar and the Mitnica settlement." Do you agree that it states that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It further states that, "Strict controls of movement within and of leaving the territory of the zone of responsibility of Operational Group South were established." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In terms of having strict controls of movement, what would that mean in practical terms, how was that done, what was your understanding?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is here defined as control of movement within the area of responsibility of the operations group, this applied throughout. There was a document from the command warning about this issue and saying that the issue should be treated in keeping with its objective importance and that's why we can read this here. This issue of control of letting people through of check-points, of police supervision of the entire territory, and movement -- movement by members of Operations Group South, and specifically here in relation to members of the Croatian forces who had surrendered. That sort of thing. One needed to have a very convincing reason for leaving one's area of responsibility or one's operations area at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It worked like this in people's minds: This thing is now over, so let's all just go home. I think that was the general line of reasoning behind this. I think this is perfectly proper, what we can see here and I think that it was done in keeping with all these rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You testified earlier that as a result of another document you had seen that check-points had been set up some time earlier before this date. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Much earlier. There were check-points along the main roads leading out of the operations area. These started functioning immediately after the arrival of the guards brigade. The regime became stricter and more specific after the 15th of October. No one was allowed in or out without a proper permit, a pass or authorisation issued by the commander himself. Nobody could leave the area. And there was no room for any misuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And further in the report it states that city commands were set up pursuant to an earlier order on the 7th of November. Can you briefly state that, read what it says in relation to those city commands. It's just above paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. "Pursuant to your order", there was another order on the 9th of November, the one that was based on this one dated the 7th of November, and now we might want to look at that again. The village of Negoslavci. Yes. This is now a report that is in relation to the commander's previous order in relation to these issues. Negoslavci, Major Vukasinovic [as interpreted] Ljubisa; village of Berak, Colonel Borisa Gluscevic; Ovcara Jakubovac Grabovo, Lieutenant-Colonel Slobodan Misovic. Upon his departure from the zone of responsibility of Operations Group South Lieutenant-Colonel Milorad Vojinovic was appointed. There you go. That's it. So this is a report on how the superior commander's orders were carried out. And further for Vucedol and Mitnica, Major Stupar for Petrova Gora and the western part of the graveyard; as far as the Vuka River, Major Borivoje Tesic; for the area between Sajmiste street east and Mitnica, Major Adem Bajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can stop you there. If we can back to the village commands that he reports that were set up or the city commanders that appears in the translation, you spoke a little fast, but in relation to the village of Negoslavci, Major Vukasinovic was appointed as the commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in relation to the village of Berak, Colonel Gluscevic, if you could pronounce that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then in the village of Ovcara, in the village of Jakubovac, and the village of Grabovo, Lieutenant-Colonel Slobodan Misovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And upon his departure from the zone of responsibility for Operational Group South, Lieutenant-Colonel Vojinovic, Milorad, was appointed. Do you agree that the document states that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So the appointment of Lieutenant-Colonel Vojinovic we relates to him as being appointed as being the city or village commander of Ovcara village, Jakubovac and Grabovo. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that's on the basis of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is a report. It's a regular report. This report is meant to inform everyone about the order, you know the previous order, but there is a new order that was produced on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Certainly this order doesn't -- when we look at these appointments of city commands, it doesn't appoint Vojinovic as commander of Operational Group South, does it? It's just a bit unclear in your earlier answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Ovcara, this is a report to the superior command. There was an order from the commander and there is the report dated 1800 hours, the 19th of November. There was an order before this report, preceding this report, in relation to the villages of Ovcara, Jakubovac and Grabovo. Lieutenant-Colonel Misovic was appointed local commander. Upon his departure from the area of responsibility of Operations Group South and upon the departure of the 20th Partisan Brigade from the area of responsibility. Since he was the commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Milorad Vojinovic was appointed on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on -- at 6.00 on the 19th of November, 1991, the date that this report was made, who was the commander of Lieutenant-Colonel Vojinovic? Who was his commander of this date, based on this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Mrksic. The commander of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we can look further down the report, under the heading the 19th of November, 1991, and this is just above paragraph 4, towards the end of the document there is a paragraph that relates to Operational Group South command was engaged in admitting a number of delegations, missions, and journalists. And it further states that at about 10.00 of the 19th a delegation of the UN mission led by Cyrus Vance, the personal representative of the UN Secretary General arrived at the Operational Group South headquarters. Do you see that in the report?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And it states that the Secretary General was interested on the activities of the liberation of Vukovar and the treatment of prisoners and the wounded. And then it follows on his visit to the Vukovar barracks. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you at that meeting with Cyrus Vance?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who else was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Mrksic, Major Sljivancanin, Colonel Gluscevic, Major Trifunovic, and Major Tatic [Realtime transcript read in error "Tadic"].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In the transcript we have Colonel Mrksic, Major Sljivancanin, yourself, and Major Tadic, but the other colonel's name wasn't recorded.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Borisa Gluscevic, it's not Major Tadic, it's Tatic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how long did that meeting take?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. But not more than 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The report states that Mr. Vance was interested in the treatment of the civilian prisoners and the wounded. Can you provide us with some more information about what his concerns were?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been a long time, although I was there at the meeting, it's still difficult for me to look back and remember all the details of our discussion. I remember the general outline. Vukovar was now under JNA control. The UN presence was established, the thing to do was to see how we could now deal with any problems that might have arisen, issues regarding prisoners, civilians, the wounded, that sort of thing. That was the subject of the meeting. The subject matter discussed. I think he was quite happy with the commander's report on the progress of operations on that last day. On the surrender of the Croatian forces and the way they were treated. Once he had received this report I remember when I look at this report and I remember how it happened, he wished to go straight to the Vukovar barracks and see for himself what exactly was going on, so he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was the specific application of the protection to the Geneva Conventions discussed in relation to civilian prisoners and combatant prisoners? If you remember. If you don't, just say so.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the subject discussed, the wounded, the patients, what to do with them, and so on and so forth. He received confirmation here that the issue had been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Continue.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Help was expected from the 1st Military District to deal with these issues, to tackle these issues. Somebody else was supposed to come along. There were other issues concerning the operations group command was not qualified to deal with all these various issues. Of course help was expected, because help had been requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what particular help was requested, and who requested it? If you know.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the guards brigade, more specifically the commander. The same applied to all sorts of logistical issues. Monitoring the transport from all sides. Also in view of the imminent evacuation of the hospital and the wounded, teams were to be sent out to deal with these steps. There must be something in the war diary about this, namely that such requests were made, either orally by the commander or by Telex, I can't quite remember. Or maybe he used our communications equipment to ask for help. I know that the war diary was kept and I know that these were the expectations. There is the order by the commander of the 1st Military District saying that logistics units would be involved in dealing with certain issues within the operations group, as well as security bodies. I think there was a document like that produced by the 1st Military District that was part of the register book that was entered there, on how the wounded were to be treated, and this was definitely something that was eventually received by the command of the guards brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in this document it states that at 1600 hours in the region of Velepromet there was a delegation of the Red Cross of Yugoslavia. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was Velepromet being used for at that stage, to your knowledge? This is on the 19th of November at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one of the facilities used to assemble people. There were people coming from various parts of the town and at that point it was impossible to separate people to the distinguish between this or that group. Therefore, they had to be collected in certain -- at certain points and what we had at our disposal was Velepromet, Ovcara and the barracks. The Red Cross delegation went to Velepromet, I presume to see what the situation was with the people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say that these were certain points that you had at "our disposal" and you refer to Velepromet and Ovcara and the barracks, who are you saying are "our" disposal, who is "our"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Operations Group. They were inside the Operations Group zone, and those facilities provided the conditions necessary to have so many people in one place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were these three places in the Operational Group South's zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document. I have provided the ERN numbers previously. Perhaps I'll give them again 0467-2869 to 0467-2871.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 418, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before we leave that document, Mr. Smith, one matter that interests the Chamber. The appointment of village and area commanders that has been referred to, in what area did Velepromet come, under whose command?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you heard the Judge's question, and earlier you talked about an order where there were village and town commands set up, and also you discussed that the order also mentioned that assault detachments were placed in areas in the town of Vukovar. Do you remember giving that evidence from the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So in relation to those town commanders and the village commanders, the commanders of the units that were placed in charge of them, which village or town command did Velepromet fall under?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it fell under the area of responsibility of the assault detachment number 2. I believe it fell under their area, and in that regard the commander of the assault detachment number 2 was responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And Assault Detachment 2, who was the commander of that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the previous commander's orders, Colonel Boja Bojat, who was the previous Operations Group South commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Branislav Lukic had been appointed on the 3rd or the 4th of October. Pursuant to that order, Major Bajic, the commander of the battalion was not replaced. I don't mean to imply that there was dual command of the Assault Detachment in place at the time, but as to why he was appointed commander for that part of Vukovar, well, I presume that's because he was a battalion commander. And as regards combat activities in the entire area of responsibility, those were commanded by Lieutenant-Colonel Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to finish this topic, the town and village commanders in place at this point at the 19th of November, 1991, who were they subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the commander who appointed them, being commander of OG South, Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- I now tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It has already been received, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to tab number 28, please. And this is 65 ter number 602. And there is a document, an order dated the 20th of November, 1991, the time is 6.00 in the morning, and it's typed at the base of the document that it's an order from Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to that order it asks that, first paragraph, "In the course of the 20th of November, 1991," it orders that the continual of the mopping up of the liberated areas and the facilities of Vukovar from the remaining parts of Ustasha formations and take measures necessary for establishing full control in the town. "Simultaneously evacuate and transport civilians, the wounded and the sick from the hospital in Vukovar." Do you see that in the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: There are other further orders that we can discuss, but in relation to the evacuation of the wounded and the sick from the hospital in Vukovar, nothing further is mentioned in that order about that activity, is there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were there any follow-up orders from Colonel Mrksic in relation to how that evacuation of civilians was to be carried out from the hospital of Vukovar, the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the existing written orders, which would specifically deal with these issues, I don't believe there were any such orders. As for any oral orders that may have been issued, I'm not familiar with those.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And paragraph 2 it states that return artillery battalions from the -- and perhaps if you can -- perhaps if you can just read out paragraph 2 in relation to the resubordination issued there, order issued.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Return artillery battalions from the 1st proletarian mechanised division of the 453rd mechanised brigade which were subordinated to the OG South to their original formations. Return AJD 105 millimetres which was supporting the OG South to the 80th Motorised Brigade formation and continue with the support pursuant to the plan of the 80th Motorised Brigade command." That was item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to the Howitzer battalion being returned to the 80th Motorised Brigade, did that originally come from the 80th Motorised Brigade, that Howitzer battalion.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether they came to the 80th Motorised Brigade? I didn't understand the question. Whether they were already under or within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: My question was, did the Howitzer battalion, was that originally with the 80th Motorised Brigade, and then, by this order, it's simply being returned?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by establishment it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And further in the order it states that all necessary measures in Operational Group South, units to -- sorry. I'll repeat that. It states, "Take all necessary measures in Operational Group South to secure and control the territory in the area of responsibility." Do you see that? And if you can read out just the last paragraph or the last sentence above paragraph 4 in relation to the responsibility of town commanders.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The town commanders in the OG South area of responsibility are to take all necessary measures for the full functioning of the military authorities, pursuant to order - strictly confidential number 349-1 of the 8th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the 9th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And this is at 6.00 in the morning on the 20th of November, 1991. At this -- at this point?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Based on this document, who was the 80th Motorised Brigade subordinated to, based on this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Operations Group South.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document. It's 65 ter number 602.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 419, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 577 and it's an order from Colonel Mrksic, the Operational Group South commander, regulating the issue of resubordination. And if you can briefly read that order out, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Regulating the issue of resubordination: Order. In order to unify command for future activities, resubordinate: The armoured battalion of the 554th Motorised Brigade to the 80th Motorised Brigade. All issues regarding resubordination will be regulated by the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade. "Until they receive a new task, the armoured battalion of the 544th Motorised Brigade will be carrying out tasks in compliance with the decision of the 16th of November, 1991."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document, and it's 65 ter number 577.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 420, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if you can turn to tab 30, please. This is 65 ter number 67. It's a report, a regular combat report from Colonel Mrksic, Operational Group South commander, and it's addressed to the 1st Military District command and the Federal Secretariat for the National Defence cabinet. And it's dated --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It's dated the 20th of November at 6.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to this report, it reports on some of the activities of Operational Group South, and would you be able to read out paragraph 1, please, as to some of the activities conducted?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE TRIFUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. [Interpretation] "Upon your request we are forwarding the report on realization of tasks. You set in your order strictly confidential number 1614-82/81 of 18 November, 1992. Since in the task to the OG South you are directed that the OG South during the morning by 1000 hours on the 19th of November, 1991, takes over the hospital and the MUP and clears Vukovar of Ustasha forces. This task was carried out by 1100 hours on the 19th of November, is you, and safe movement through town and control protection service were secured. The clearing up of the Mitnica settlement and certain streets and buildings in the centre of Vukovar continued."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I have some further questions about that topic. It's a quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Smith. Yes. We resume tomorrow at 9.30 in the morning. We will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of May, 2006, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
